statements.status_notes: jackson-databind's deserializer for java.nio.file.Path resolves an attacker-supplied URI without restricting the URI scheme. In JDKFromStringDeserializer.NioPathHelper.deserialize, a string bound from untrusted JSON is passed to new URI(value) and then to Path.of(uri). When that throws FileSystemNotFoundException, the code enumerates ServiceLoader<FileSystemProvider> and calls provider.getPath(uri) on the first provider whose scheme matches the attacker-chosen scheme. Untrusted JSON can therefore select and drive an arbitrary registered FileSystemProvider during readValue under a default JsonMapper, and forces provider class loading at the same time. With only the JDK built-in providers (file, jar/zipfs) present, the resolved path is inert and no mount or network I/O occurs; further impact requires a side-effecting third-party FileSystemProvider on the classpath. This affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 2.8.0 before 2.18.10, from 2.19.0 before 2.21.6, and from 2.22.0 before 2.22.2, and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 before 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 before 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2, 3.1.6, or 3.2.2. Binding java.nio.file.Path from untrusted JSON should be avoided regardless of version.
statements.impact_statement: The same advisory covers the Jackson 3 coordinate, which is a separate artifact from com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind and carries its own version line, so it is assessed here rather than folded into the Jackson 2 entry. Jackson 3 appears in two places in the Liquibase Secure distribution: relocated inside liquibase-commercial-cassandra on the current main build (3.2.2, already fixed) and inside the liquibase-license-tracking application (3.2.1). The reachability argument is the same as for Jackson 2 and holds independently of version: the vulnerable NioPathHelper path runs only when Jackson binds a JSON string into a java.nio.file.Path target, either directly or through a bean that declares a Path-typed property. An inspection of every jar in the shipped distribution, including the Jackson copies relocated inside the couchbase, databricks and snowflake drivers and the license-tracking application, found no Jackson-bound class with a Path-typed property. The classes that reference both Path and Jackson (the Snowflake and Databricks token caches and config parsers, Couchbase's ImportFile, Liquibase's ProJsonChangeLogParser, the Jackson 3 stream factories) use Path as a file handle for the document being read and bind its content into Map, JsonNode or their own DTOs without Path fields. Liquibase Secure's own Jackson call sites bind into Object or Map.

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.0.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, JDKFromStringDeserializer constructed InetSocketAddress with new InetSocketAddress(host, port), which performs eager DNS name resolution for hostname inputs at deserialization time. An application that binds untrusted JSON into a type containing an InetSocketAddress field issues an attacker-chosen DNS query during readValue, before any application-level validation or connect logic. The fix uses InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved(host, port), deferring DNS to an explicit connect. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.
statements.impact_statement: The same advisory covers the Jackson 3 coordinate, which is a separate artifact with its own version line. Fixed in tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.4. The only in-range copies are inside the license-tracking application archived under /liquibase/dist in Docker images 5.1.0 (3.0.4), 5.1.1 (3.1.0) and 5.2.0 (3.1.2), read from the jars' Maven metadata. Images 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 carry 3.2.0 and 3.2.1 there, 6.0.0 carries 3.2.2 inside liquibase-commercial-cassandra, and the 5.0.x images carry no Jackson 3; all of these are outside the range. Liquibase's own code does not use Jackson 3. This assessment does not rest on version. The license-tracking application is a Spring Boot 4 service that must be extracted and started by hand. It binds the request body of its track endpoint with Jackson 3, to plain classes made of strings, booleans, dates, a string map and nested user records. None of those classes has an InetSocketAddress field, so the eager DNS lookup in the deserializer is never triggered.

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.21.0 until 2.21.4 and 3.1.4, POJOPropertiesCollector._renameProperties() allows a property with @JsonProperty("renamed") on the getter and @JsonIgnore on the setter to be renamed rather than dropped. With MapperFeature.INFER_PROPERTY_MUTATORS enabled (default), the private backing field is retained; during deserialization BeanDeserializerFactory.addBeanProps() sees hasField()==true, builds a FieldProperty, and makes the backing field writable. An attacker supplying the renamed JSON key writes the backing field directly, bypassing the @JsonIgnore on the setter. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.21.4 and 3.1.4.

From 2.21.0 until 2.21.4 and 3.1.4, in BeanDeserializer._deserializeUsingPropertyBased, the active-view (@JsonView) filter was applied only to creator properties; the regular property-buffering branch performed no prop.visibleInView(activeView) check. A change making SetterlessProperty.isMerging() return true routed setterless Collection/Map properties through this unguarded path, so a setterless collection annotated with a restricted @JsonView is populated from attacker JSON even when the active view excludes it. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.21.4 and 3.1.4.

From 2.21.0 until 2.21.4 and 3.1.4, UnwrappedPropertyHandler.processUnwrappedCreatorProperties() replays buffered JSON into creator parameters but never consults prop.visibleInView(activeView). statements.status_notes: jackson-databind binds a JSON string to a javax.xml.datatype.Duration or javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar field by passing the raw string verbatim to DatatypeFactory.newDuration(value) or newXMLGregorianCalendar(value). These deserializers are registered by default with no opt-in. The XML Schema lexical grammar permits numeric components of arbitrary length, which the JDK materializes through the native BigInteger(String) and BigDecimal(String) constructors, both quadratic in digit count, and because the digits sit inside a JSON string token rather than a JSON number token the maxNumberLength guard never applies. This affects tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 before 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 before 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 3.1.6 or 3.2.2.
statements.impact_statement: The same advisory covers the Jackson 3 coordinate, which is a separate artifact from com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind and carries its own version line, so it is assessed here rather than folded into the Jackson 2 entry. Liquibase Secure ships one Jackson 3 copy, in liquibase-commercial-cassandra, and it is on the fixed 3.2.2. That was read out of the built distribution rather than from the dependency graph: internal/extensions/liquibase-commercial-cassandra.jar carries META-INF/maven/tools.jackson.core/jackson-databind/pom.properties with version=3.2.2, and the constant in tools/jackson/databind/cfg/PackageVersion agrees. jackson-core in the same jar is also 3.2.2. The reachability argument is the same as for Jackson 2 and holds independently of the version: no production code in this repository references javax.xml.datatype.Duration or XMLGregorianCalendar, so the XML datatype deserializers that carry the unbounded parse are never given a target to bind. One thing to watch rather than a present exposure: no POM here pins tools.jackson.core. The version arrives transitively from com.ing.data:cassandra-jdbc-wrapper, pinned at 5.0.3 via cassandra-jdbc.version, and only that release carries a fixed Jackson. Wrapper 5.0.2 and 5.0.1 declare 3.2.0 and wrapper 5.0.0 declares 3.1.3, both inside the affected ranges, so a wrapper change could reintroduce an affected copy with no POM edit here to signal it.

statements.status_notes: DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator is the PolymorphicTypeValidator applied automatically whenever @JsonTypeInfo is used without an explicitly configured custom validator. It denies polymorphic resolution only for a fixed set of "unsafe base types", and its isSafeSubType method returns true unconditionally for every base type outside that set. java.lang.Comparable was absent from the list despite being implemented by a very large fraction of JDK and application classes, comparable in breadth to java.io.Serializable, which is on the list for that reason. An application declaring an @JsonTypeInfo-annotated property or class with Comparable as its base type, and no custom PolymorphicTypeValidator, will accept a type identifier for essentially any class implementing Comparable. This yields an attacker-controlled object instantiation primitive; a demonstrated case constructs a java.io.File for an arbitrary attacker-chosen path, which becomes path-traversal-adjacent if the application subsequently calls path-sensitive methods on the value. No class implementing Comparable has been identified that yields code execution through deserialization alone. Global Default Typing via activateDefaultTyping is not affected, because that method structurally requires an explicit PolymorphicTypeValidator argument. This affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 2.11.0 before 2.18.10, from 2.19.0 before 2.21.6, and from 2.22.0 before 2.22.2, and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 before 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 before 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2, 3.1.6, or 3.2.2.
statements.impact_statement: The same advisory covers the Jackson 3 coordinate, which is a separate artifact from com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind and carries its own version line, so it is assessed here rather than folded into the Jackson 2 entry. Jackson 3 appears in two places in the Liquibase Secure distribution: relocated inside liquibase-commercial-cassandra on the current main build (3.2.2, already fixed) and inside the liquibase-license-tracking application (3.2.1). The reachability argument is the same as for Jackson 2 and holds independently of version: the vulnerable DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator path is exercised only when an application declares @JsonTypeInfo on a property or class whose base type is java.lang.Comparable and lets Jackson fall back to the default validator. An inspection of every jar in the shipped distribution, including the Jackson copies relocated inside the couchbase, databricks and snowflake drivers and the license-tracking application, found @JsonTypeInfo declared on exactly three base types, Apache Arrow's ArrowType (bundled by bigquery, databricks and snowflake) and Couchbase's AnalyticsLink and BucketConfig, plus a reflective lookup of the annotation in Azure Core's FlatteningDeserializer. None of these base types is Comparable, and all of them bind JSON that comes from the respective database or cloud service, not from Liquibase users. Liquibase Secure's own code never uses @JsonTypeInfo.

statements.status_notes: TypeDeserializerBase._findDeserializer() in FasterXML jackson-databind caches the resolved deserializer under the raw, attacker-supplied type ID. When name-based polymorphism is configured with a fallback, for example @JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.NAME, defaultImpl = ...), every distinct unrecognized type ID resolves to the same fallback deserializer but is retained as its own key in the _deserializers map. That map has no configurable bound and lives for the lifetime of the type deserializer, so an attacker who can repeatedly supply fresh unknown type IDs causes monotonic memory retention across requests. Exploitation requires an application that enables name-based polymorphism with a defaultImpl or equivalent fallback, accepts attacker-influenced type IDs, and reuses a long-lived ObjectMapper across requests. This affects tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 through 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 through 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 3.1.7 or 3.2.3.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.7 and 3.2.3. Two components ship Jackson 3. The 6.0.0 image carries one copy at 3.2.2, inside liquibase-commercial-cassandra, read from its PackageVersion class. The license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist and removed in 6.0.0, carries 3.0.4 in 5.1.0, 3.1.0 in 5.1.1, 3.1.2 in 5.2.0, 3.2.0 in 5.2.1 and 3.2.1 in 5.2.2. All of these are inside the advisory range, so this assessment does not rest on version. The vulnerable cache is filled only through name-based polymorphic typing with a fallback, such as @JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.NAME, defaultImpl = ...), applied to attacker-chosen type IDs. A scan of every class in that jar, the Cassandra driver and JDBC wrapper included, found no @JsonTypeInfo, @JsonSubTypes or default typing. The license-tracking application's own classes use only @JsonCreator, @JsonProperty and @JsonFormat, never @JsonTypeInfo or default typing. Liquibase's own code does not use Jackson 3. With no polymorphic type handling configured for Jackson 3, no type-ID cache is ever created.

statements.status_notes: Forward-reference completion for @JsonIdentityInfo object IDs in FasterXML jackson-databind performs a linear scan of the pending-reference accumulator for every resolved ID. The affected paths are CollectionDeserializer.CollectionReferringAccumulator. resolveForwardReference() and the equivalent implementation in MapDeserializer. When a document first creates N unresolved object-ID references in an identity-enabled collection or map and then defines those same IDs in reverse order, completion performs on the order of N * (N + 1) / 2 identity comparisons, so a shallow document whose size grows linearly causes quadratic CPU work during deserialization. Exploitation requires an application that deserializes attacker-influenced JSON into an identity-enabled collection or map. This affects tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 through 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 through 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 3.1.7 or 3.2.3.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.7 and 3.2.3. Two components ship Jackson 3. The 6.0.0 image carries one copy at 3.2.2, inside liquibase-commercial-cassandra, read from its PackageVersion class. The license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist and removed in 6.0.0, carries 3.0.4 in 5.1.0, 3.1.0 in 5.1.1, 3.1.2 in 5.2.0, 3.2.0 in 5.2.1 and 3.2.1 in 5.2.2. All of these are inside the advisory range, so this assessment does not rest on version. The quadratic lookup runs only when JSON is deserialized into a collection or map of @JsonIdentityInfo-enabled values. Liquibase's own code does not use Jackson 3. With no object identity configured, the forward-reference accumulator is never created.
